new_findings.text: A fourth combat-tuning divergence between the two builds, inside the boss/duelist setLevel path. Android bands boss stats at x1.25 (lvl>70), x1.2 (lvl>50), x1.1 (lvl>30) and x0.8 (lvl<10); web v0.717 bands only x1.1 (30 < lvl < 80) and x0.9 (lvl < 10). Web also sets a field to 10 * lvl that android's setLevel has no counterpart for. The boss HP half (max(levelScaledAuthoredHP, playerhit * hitsToKillBoss) with the four playerhit floors) IS identical in both.

The web form is the coherent one.

new_findings.text: The reload/focus meter constants also split by build, and the footage selects the web set — the cleanest cross-build parity datum in the repo. Web: maxreload = 8*24 = 192, HUD fraction (reload-48)/(192-48) = 144 ticks of visible travel = 6.000 s at 24.0 fps. Android: maxreload = 5*24 = 120, HUD fraction (reload-24)/(120-24) = 96 ticks = 4.000 s. Refill is +1 per frame unconditionally in both (web §1t99s0§.as:1205, android MCSPlayer.as:1160), so fill time is SPD-independent. The frame-measured fill is 45.0 px/s across a 268 px track = 5.96-6.00 s, which matches the WEB constants and rules out the android ones by 2 seconds.

new_findings.text: InputManager.maxDistance = 200 is a compile-time initialiser, not a gameplay base. setStance calls InputManager.setMaxDistance(slashLength) on every battle init for the local player (web §1t99s0§.as:3156-3158, android MCSPlayer.as:3092-3094), so the 200 is overwritten before the player ever draws a stroke. Any derivation of the wiki's 300/200/100 that treats 200 as 'the shipped default slash budget' rests on a value the player never plays at. The real base is 120 + floor((90 + 5*DAN) * SPD / (20 + SPD)) — 124 at SPD 1 / dan 0, asymptotically 210 at dan 0.

new_findings.text: EVERY 'stage px' NUMBER IN docs/research/fidelity/COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS.md THAT WAS CONVERTED AT /1.875 IS 20% TOO LARGE. The correct 1080p divisor is 2.25. The web build's letterbox routine sets base 800x480 and, for a viewport wider than 800/480 = 1.6667, takes the fit-height branch: scale = stageHeight/480 and offsetX = (stageWidth - 800*scale)/2. At 1920x1080 that is scale 2.25 with 60 px pillarbox bars. Three independent confirmations: (1) source, §1t1540s0§.as:271-307 plus §1t1523s0§.as:104/106 (stageWidth 800, stageHeight 480); (2) frames -- I measured the pillarbox on four session11 frames (first/last column with any pixel >12): damage-ttk/t125.350.png 54->1862, gap-focus-trigger/t1747.000.png 48->1867, stance-reach/B_t783.400_LIGHT_stroke-anchored-at-body_farGap436px.png 52->1868, stance-reach/A_t117.400_BALANCED_lvl1_stroke235px.png 54->1863, i.e. content ~1810-1820 px = 800x2.25 = 1800 plus compression bleed, whereas /1.875 demands 210 px black bars that are simply not present; (3) reductio -- the HUD reload bar sits at row y=1036 (I measured it), which at /1.875 maps to stage y ~504, off the bottom of a 480-tall stage, physically impossible, while at /2.25 it maps to stage y ~460 of 480, i.e. the bottom HUD strip. Corrected c-2 reach bands: LIGHT 233-241 -> 194-201 (max 303 -> 252); BALANCED 116-131 -> 97-109; HEAVY 97-103 -> 81-86 (max 121 -> 101). Note the corrected Heavy MAX of 101 now kisses the source's hard 100-px floor, and every band sits at or below its source cap, which is what a body-to-endpoint distance should do against a path-length budget.
